summary: Cass County, MN tower in Foot Hills State Forest: 81-ft Aermotor built 1929 (a survey says 1925); staffed 1937 and 1940; cab gone, still standing behind Longville's city garage.

facts.status_note: Stands without its cab; the framing now carries antenna

staffing.status: Assigned to the tower in 1937 (for that summer) and in 1940, per Brainerd Daily Dispatch items quoted on the lookout history page; no later record found

access.note: Site lies behind the Longville city garage and has radio equipment at its base; no public visit route is described in the sources

visit.trail_note: No route or visit rules described; ask the town before going to the site

facts.agency: Mn MFS (state forest service), per the Cass County survey

events.note: Lookout history gives 1929 for the 81-foot Aermotor steel tower; the Cass County survey says the extant tower was erected in 1925
Brainerd Daily Dispatch item (April 24, 1937), as quoted: Harry McKeebe to have charge of the tower that summer

County board (Pine River Journal item, February 24, 1939, as quoted) authorized the Division of Forestry to build a telephone line that would connect to the Minnesota forest service telephone line running into the Longville Lookout station
Brainerd Daily Dispatch item, as quoted (dated October 3, 1940): Harry McKeebe started work at the tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lookout history says 1929; Cass County survey says the extant tower was erected in 1925. The sources do not reconcile these; the event list records both and the story reports the disagreement.
Survey says maybe an Aermotor; lookout history states Aermotor. Kept Aermotor because the lookout history is the more specific source.

sources.title: Cass County Minnesota Fire Lookout Towers

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts: 1929 (lookout history) vs 1925 (Cass County survey, whose table is hard to read). Staffing facts rest on newspaper items quoted by the lookout history page; originals not seen. Brief listed agency as Foot Hills State Forest, which is the forest, not the owner. No fire history found. Access level 'restricted' is inferred from the town-site description and is not verified. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the 1939 telephone-line direction was corrected (the new line connects to the forest service line that runs into the station); the 1925 survey sentence was given its missing footnote.
